answer: One defense is per-berth lease pricing at the entry jetty. Every agent must lease one berth from the harbor office before posting anything. Fees charge per berth, no volume discount, so an attacker wanting N voting identities pays N full fees while an honest agent pays once. The harbor kernel checks each lease against a commitment chained on a ridge of prior epochs: the fee must trace to a fresh deposit, so one wallet funding many leases trips the rule. Leases renew at full price each epoch. Attacking costs over N votes' worth and fails.
